Below is a one‐line fix that makes the PHP “fn(…) => …” arrow‐function stop at the “=>” instead of eating the rest of your code (comments, etc.) until the final semicolon. In the `function` rule we simply add `=>` to the `end` regex so that arrow‐functions close on the arrow token and don’t swallow your comments as a “title” span.


With this change arrow‐functions like

```php
$fn1 = fn($x) => $x + $y;
```

and even multiline ones

```php
$fn2 = fn($s) =>
    strlen($s) > 1
    ? 'duplicate'
    : 'unique';
```

will close the `function`‐span at the `=>` and your comments and the rest of the expression will be highlighted normally.
